# PERSONALIZED ASTROLOGY ANALYSIS REPORT — MASTER TEMPLATE
## "The Celestial Blueprint" Report Series
### Prepared from: Birth Date · Birth Time · Birth Location

---

# FRONT MATTER

## 0.1 Cover Page
- Client name, birth data (date, exact time, city/region/country, time zone, coordinates)
- Report title, generation date, astrologer/analyst name & credentials
- Edition type: Full Three-Part Report (Birth Chart + Synastry + 12-Month Transits)

## 0.2 How to Read This Report
- Plain-language note: no prior astrology knowledge assumed
- Glossary preview (sign, planet, house, aspect, transit, orb, retrograde, element, modality)
- Disclaimer: for self-reflection and guidance purposes; not medical, legal, or financial advice
- Personalization methodology note: report computed from natal chart derived from the three data points supplied (date, time, place); explain why birth *time* matters (sets the Ascendant and house cusps)

## 0.3 Your Natal Chart at a Glance
- Wheel graphic of the birth chart
- Data table: Planet | Sign | Degree | House | Major Aspects
- Big Three summary box (one sentence each for Sun, Moon, Rising)
- Dominant element & modality quick-read
- Chart signature sentence (e.g., "A pragmatic Earth Sun, emotionally intuitive Water Moon, with a socially magnetic Air Rising")

---

# PART ONE — THE BIRTH CHART: WHO YOU ARE
*(Personality Overview)*

## SECTION 1 — THE FOUNDATION: WHY THE "TOP THREE" MATTER
### 1.0 Purpose of This Section
Explain that the Sun, Moon, and Ascendant (Rising) form the essential skeleton of the personality; every other placement adds detail to this core triad.

### 1.1 The Sun — Your Core Self
- What it represents: ego, identity, life purpose, conscious will, vitality
- Why it's the "headline" of the chart
- How the Sun sign expresses itself (element + modality + ruler)
- Interpretation block for the client's Sun: sign, house placement, aspects to the Sun
- Reflection prompts ("Where do I feel most myself? What am I becoming?")

### 1.2 The Moon — Your Inner World
- What it represents: emotions, instincts, subconscious patterns, needs, comfort habits, mothering/nurturing style, reaction patterns
- Why the Moon often explains *how you feel* even when the Sun explains *who you are*
- Interpretation block: Moon sign, house, aspects (especially Moon–Saturn, Moon–Neptune, Moon–Pluto for emotional depth work)
- Reflection prompts ("What soothes me? What triggers me? What do I need to feel safe?")

### 1.3 The Ascendant (Rising Sign) — Your Lens & Your Doorway
- What it represents: first impressions, physical presentation, approach to life, the "mask" that becomes the self, and the chart's house structure (1st house cusp)
- Why Rising changes roughly every 2 hours → importance of accurate birth time
- The Rising sign's ruler as "chart ruler" — where it sits and what that means
- Interpretation block: Rising sign, chart ruler placement, planets near the 1st house
- Reflection prompts ("How do others see me before they know me? How do I meet the world?")

### 1.4 The Big Three as a System
- How Sun/Moon/Rising interact (e.g., a fire Sun with a water Moon = passion filtered through sensitivity)
- The "three masks" model: Sun = who I am becoming · Moon = who I've always been · Rising = who I appear to be
- Harmony and tension between the three (using aspects between Sun, Moon, and chart ruler)
- One-paragraph integrated "Big Three Portrait" written specifically for the client

---

## SECTION 2 — PLANETARY PLACEMENTS: THE FULL INNER CAST
*(For each planet: what it rules → what its sign means → what its house means → key aspects → plain-English summary → reflection prompt)*

### 2.1 Mercury — Mind & Communication
- Themes: thinking style, learning, speech, writing, decision-making, siblings/local travel
- Sign placement meaning → House placement meaning → Aspects (esp. Mercury–Uranus, Mercury–Neptune, Mercury–Saturn)

### 2.2 Venus — Love, Values & Pleasure
- Themes: attraction, affection style, aesthetics, money values, what you find beautiful
- Sign → House → Aspects (Venus–Mars for desire style; Venus–Saturn for commitment lessons)

### 2.3 Mars — Drive, Action & Desire
- Themes: motivation, anger style, courage, sexuality, assertion, how you pursue goals
- Sign → House → Aspects (Mars–Saturn for frustration/ambition; Mars–Pluto for intensity)

### 2.4 Jupiter — Growth, Belief & Opportunity
- Themes: optimism, philosophy, abundance patterns, luck, teaching/learning, travel
- Sign → House → Aspects (Jupiter–Neptune for idealism; Jupiter–Saturn for realism)

### 2.5 Saturn — Structure, Lessons & Mastery
- Themes: discipline, fear, responsibility, maturity, career pressure, life's "curriculum"
- Sign → House → Aspects (Saturn–Pluto for power struggles; Saturn–Neptune for doubt vs. faith)

### 2.6 Uranus — Freedom, Innovation & Awakening
- Themes: rebellion, originality, sudden change, individuation, technology
- Sign → House → Aspects (Uranus–Sun/Moon for identity breakthroughs)

### 2.7 Neptune — Imagination, Spirituality & Illusion
- Themes: dreams, intuition, compassion, glamour, escapism, creative channel
- Sign → House → Aspects (Neptune–Venus for romance idealization; Neptune–Mercury for creative mind)

### 2.8 Pluto — Power, Transformation & Depth
- Themes: regeneration, obsession, control dynamics, psychological rebirth, shared resources
- Sign → House → Aspects (Pluto–Moon for emotional intensity; Pluto–Sun for empowerment arcs)

### 2.9 The Lunar Nodes — Destiny Direction
- North Node: soul growth direction; South Node: inherited gifts and karmic comfort zone
- Node sign + house, with the "move from South to North" life narrative

### 2.10 Chiron — The Wounded Healer (Optional Add-On)
- Core wound, healing gift, where you help others through your own pain
- Sign, house, and aspects to personal planets

### 2.11 Angles Deep Dive
- IC (roots, home, ancestry) · Descendant (what you project onto partners) · MC (public life, career, reputation)
- Planets conjunct angles as outsized life themes

### 2.12 Planet-in-House Master Grid
A reference table: all 10 planets × their houses, with a one-line "life area" interpretation for each (this satisfies the requirement for planetary placements and their meanings *in each house* — presented both narratively above and as a quick-reference grid here).

---

## SECTION 3 — THE FOUR ELEMENTS: BALANCE & IMBALANCE IN YOUR CHART
*(Concluding section of the Birth Chart report)*

### 3.0 How Elements Are Counted
- Weighting methodology: Sun, Moon, Rising, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto, plus house concentration and chart shape
- Client's element tally table (e.g., Fire 3 · Earth 5 · Air 1 · Water 4)

### 3.1 Fire (Aries, Leo, Sagittarius) — Inspiration & Will
- **Balanced expression:** enthusiasm, confidence, initiative, warmth, visionary energy
- **Excess Fire:** impulsiveness, burnout, self-centeredness, difficulty listening, arrogance
- **Lack of Fire:** low motivation, difficulty self-starting, muted passion, needing external spark
- **Balancing advice** if excessive or lacking (people, habits, environments to seek)

### 3.2 Earth (Taurus, Virgo, Capricorn) — Practicality & Stability
- **Balanced:** groundedness, reliability, sensory pleasure, patience, tangible results
- **Excess Earth:** rigidity, materialism, stubbornness, overwork, resistance to change
- **Lack of Earth:** impracticality, difficulty finishing things, poor boundaries with money/body, disorganization
- **Balancing advice**

### 3.3 Air (Gemini, Libra, Aquarius) — Intellect & Connection
- **Balanced:** curiosity, communication, objectivity, social ease, adaptability
- **Excess Air:** overthinking, detachment from emotion, gossip, indecision, living "in the head"
- **Lack of Air:** difficulty articulating ideas, discomfort with abstraction, resistance to other perspectives
- **Balancing advice**

### 3.4 Water (Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces) — Emotion & Intuition
- **Balanced:** empathy, intuition, emotional depth, creativity, healing presence
- **Excess Water:** moodiness, emotional flooding, victimhood, boundary loss, escapism
- **Lack of Water:** emotional restraint, difficulty accessing feelings, disconnect from intuition, perceived coldness
- **Balancing advice**

### 3.5 Modality Quick-Read (Cardinal · Fixed · Mutable)
- Brief balance note for each modality and its excess/lack patterns

### 3.6 Your Element Portrait
- Synthesis paragraph: dominant element as superpower, lacking element as growth edge
- One actionable practice per imbalance (journaling prompt, habit, environment tweak)
- Closing narrative paragraph that ties Sun/Moon/Rising and element balance together

---
---

# PART TWO — SYNASTRY & RELATIONSHIP BLUEPRINT: WHAT TO LOOK FOR
*(Equal emphasis on FRIENDS and PARTNERS)*

## SECTION 4 — READING OTHER PEOPLE'S CHARTS AGAINST YOURS
### 4.0 What Synastry Is (and Isn't)
- Overlay method explanation: their planets on your houses (and vice versa)
- Soulmate/soul-clash is a spectrum — all charts show growth potential
- Note: this section also functions as a standalone "what to look for" checklist when you don't yet have a specific person's chart

### 4.1 Your Relationship Wiring (Natal Foundations)
- Venus sign/house: how you love and what you value in others
- Mars sign/house: how you pursue and what excites you
- Moon sign/house: emotional needs in closeness
- 5th house (romance/play) vs. 7th house (partnership) vs. 11th house (friendship/community) rulers
- Descendant sign: the qualities you project onto "the other"

## SECTION 5 — WHAT TO LOOK FOR IN A ROMANTIC PARTNER
### 5.1 Core Compatibility Markers
- **Sun–Sun:** identity resonance (conjunction, trine, sextile = ease; square/opposition = polarity and spark)
- **Moon–Moon:** emotional compatibility (the single best indicator of day-to-day harmony)
- **Venus–Mars:** romantic/sexual chemistry
- **Sun–Moon:** classic "marriage aspect" interplay
- **Venus–Venus:** shared values and affection style

### 5.2 Deeper Currents
- **Saturn contacts:** commitment, maturity, but also heaviness/obligation
- **Pluto contacts:** intensity, transformation, power dynamics
- **Neptune contacts:** glamour and spiritual connection vs. projection and disillusionment
- **Uranus contacts:** excitement and freedom vs. instability
- **Chiron contacts:** healing through the relationship
- **Nodes contacts:** fated-feeling bonds

### 5.3 House Overlays That Matter for Romance
- Their planets in your 5th (romance), 7th (commitment), 8th (intimacy/shared resources), 4th (home/family)
- Your planets in their houses (reciprocity check)

### 5.4 Red Flags & Growth Edges
- Hard Moon–Saturn (emotional coldness), Mars–Pluto (control), Venus–Neptune (idealization), Mercury–Mars (arguments)
- How to phrase challenges constructively (every hard aspect = a skill to build)

### 5.5 Your Ideal Partner Profile
- 5–7 bullet synthesis drawn from Sections 5.1–5.4
- "Green flags" checklist for early dating

## SECTION 6 — WHAT TO LOOK FOR IN FRIENDS (EQUAL EMPHASIS)
### 6.1 Friendship Is Its Own Architecture
- Why 11th-house overlays and Air-sign connections matter as much as romance markers
- Friendships as chosen family: the Moon, Mercury, and Jupiter connections

### 6.2 Core Friendship Compatibility Markers
- **Mercury–Mercury / Mercury–Sun:** easy conversation, mutual understanding
- **Moon–Venus / Moon–Jupiter:** warmth, comfort, emotional generosity
- **Sun–Jupiter:** mutual encouragement and celebration
- **Venus–Venus:** shared taste, activities, and values
- **Jupiter–Jupiter:** shared philosophy, humor, worldview
- **Saturn (soft aspects):** loyalty, reliability, "ride or die" endurance

### 6.3 The Friendship Houses
- Their planets in your 3rd (daily connection), 5th (fun/creativity), 9th (beliefs/adventure), 11th (community/groups)
- Group dynamics: 11th-house stelliums and community leadership
- The "friend who becomes family" signature (Moon, IC, or Node contacts)

### 6.4 Friendship Red Flags & Growth Edges
- Hard Mercury–Mercury (constant misunderstanding), Moon–Mars (emotional reactivity), Jupiter–Neptune (enabling/enabling illusions), Saturn hard aspects (criticism, one-sided obligation)
- How to name and repair friendship friction using the chart as a mirror

### 6.5 Your Ideal Friend Profile
- 5–7 bullet synthesis drawn from Sections 6.2–6.4
- "Green flags" checklist for new friendships
- Explicit note: friendship analysis receives equal weight to romantic analysis — because community shapes a life as much as a partner does

## SECTION 7 — SYNTHESIS: YOUR RELATIONSHIP BLUEPRINT
- Side-by-side comparison table: Partner Markers vs. Friend Markers (planet pairs, houses, quality of connection)
- Patterns to watch across *all* relationship types (recurring aspects, repeated hard/easy themes)
- Timing note: when to expect relationship themes to activate (link to Part Three transits)
- Reflection prompts for both romantic and platonic growth

---
---

# PART THREE — 12-MONTH TRANSIT FORECAST: THE YEAR AHEAD
*(Personalized predictions written in weekly increments)*

## SECTION 8 — HOW YOUR FORECAST IS BUILT
### 8.0 Transit Method
- Current planetary positions compared to your natal chart
- Major transits highlighted (Saturn, Jupiter, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto, eclipses, Mercury/Venus/Mars retrogrades)
- Orb and timing conventions; "orb of influence" note (events may color a window, not a single day)

### 8.1 Your Year at a Glance
- 12-month calendar heat map (intensity by week)
- Major transit timeline (dates, planet, natal point touched, theme)
- Eclipse seasons and retrograde periods flagged
- 3–5 headline themes for the year

## SECTION 9 — WEEKLY FORECAST (WEEKS 1–52)
*Each weekly entry follows the same mini-template:*

> **WEEK [N] · [Date Range] · Theme of the Week**
> - **Sky This Week:** key transits & lunar phase
> - **For You:** how it lands on your natal chart (personalized)
> - **Focus Area:** career / relationships / health / money / home / creativity (rotate as relevant)
> - **Best Day(s):** and **Caution Day(s)**
> - **One Action Step:** concrete, doable within 7 days
> - **Reflection Prompt:** a single question

### 9.1 Month 1 — Weeks 1–4 (rolling 12 months from report generation date)
*(Insert 4 weekly entries in the mini-template format above, e.g.:)*
- **Week 1 · [start–end date] · Theme: Seeding Intentions** — Sky: [transits]; For You: [natal application]; Focus: personal goals; Best Day; Caution Day; Action Step; Reflection Prompt.
- **Week 2 · Theme: [derived from transits]**
- **Week 3 · Theme: [derived from transits]**
- **Week 4 · Theme: [derived from transits]**

### 9.2 Month 2 — Weeks 5–8
*(4 weekly entries, same format)*

### 9.3 Month 3 — Weeks 9–12
*(4 weekly entries, same format; flag eclipse season or retrograde if applicable)*

### 9.4 Month 4 — Weeks 13–16
*(4 weekly entries, same format)*

### 9.5 Month 5 — Weeks 17–20
*(4 weekly entries, same format)*

### 9.6 Month 6 — Weeks 21–24
*(4 weekly entries, same format; mid-year checkpoint note)*

### 9.7 Month 7 — Weeks 25–28
*(4 weekly entries, same format)*

### 9.8 Month 8 — Weeks 29–32
*(4 weekly entries, same format)*

### 9.9 Month 9 — Weeks 33–36
*(4 weekly entries, same format; flag second eclipse season or retrograde if applicable)*

### 9.10 Month 10 — Weeks 37–40
*(4 weekly entries, same format)*

### 9.11 Month 11 — Weeks 41–44
*(4 weekly entries, same format)*

### 9.12 Month 12 — Weeks 45–48
*(4 weekly entries, same format)*

### 9.13 Weeks 49–52 — Closing the Year
*(4 weekly entries, same format; include year-in-review prompt and intention-setting for the following cycle)*

**Weekly format notes for report generation:**
- Every week must include: date range, week number, theme title, sky summary, personalized natal application, focus area, best/caution days, one action step, one reflection prompt.
- Themes are derived from the dominant transit of the week (e.g., "Week 12 · Mercury Retrograde in Your 3rd House · Theme: Rework, Don't Rush").
- Retrograde weeks must include a specific "revisit/revise" instruction.
- Eclipse weeks must include a "closure and reset" instruction.
- Weeks with no major transits use lunar phase + personal house activity for the theme ("Integration Week").

## SECTION 10 — QUARTERLY DEEP DIVES
### 10.1 Quarter 1 Review (Weeks 1–13)
- Major themes, key dates, relationship vs. career vs. personal-growth balance, one big question to sit with

### 10.2 Quarter 2 Review (Weeks 14–26)
*(same structure)*

### 10.3 Quarter 3 Review (Weeks 27–39)
*(same structure)*

### 10.4 Quarter 4 Review (Weeks 40–52)
*(same structure)*

## SECTION 11 — YEAR-END SYNTHESIS
- 3 overarching predictions for the year with timing windows
- Personal growth arc narrative (beginning → middle → end of the year)
- Recommended focus rhythm: when to push, when to rest, when to consolidate
- Suggested annual ritual: birth-chart anniversary journaling prompt

---
---

# BACK MATTER

## A. Appendices
- A1: Full glossary of terms
- A2: Planet-by-sign quick reference (all 10 planets × 12 signs)
- A3: Planet-by-house quick reference (all 10 planets × 12 houses)
- A4: Aspect quick reference (conjunction, sextile, square, trine, opposition, quincunx)
- A5: Element & modality tables
- A6: Retrograde calendar for the forecast year
- A7: Eclipse calendar for the forecast year

## B. Data & Method
- Chart calculation settings (house system used, zodiac used, orb settings)
- Time zone and daylight-saving corrections applied
- Confidence note on birth-time accuracy and its effect on Rising sign/house cusps

## C. Next Steps
- Optional add-ons: full compatibility report with a named person, progressed chart, solar return, yearly re-subscription
- Contact/booking information
- Feedback prompt

---

# TEMPLATE STRUCTURE SUMMARY (for report generation)

| Part | Section | Content | Requirement Covered |
|------|---------|---------|---------------------|
| Front Matter | 0.1–0.3 | Cover, how-to-read, chart at a glance | Setup |
| Birth Chart | 1.1–1.4 | Sun, Moon, Rising + integrated Big Three portrait | "Top three" importance section |
| Birth Chart | 2.1–2.12 | Planetary placements + house meanings + aspects + grid | Detailed planetary placements by house |
| Birth Chart | 3.1–3.6 | Four elements: excess and lack meanings + balancing advice | Element overview concluding birth chart |
| Synastry | 4–5 | What to look for in partners (romantic) | Partner emphasis |
| Synastry | 6 | What to look for in friends (equal weight, mirror structure) | Friend emphasis equal to partners |
| Synastry | 7 | Combined relationship blueprint | Balance across relationship types |
| Transits | 8–9 | Method + 52 weekly forecast entries (Weeks 1–52) | Weekly increments for the next year |
| Transits | 10–11 | Quarterly deep dives + year synthesis | Personalized predictions |
| Back Matter | A–C | Appendices, method, next steps | Completeness |

Done — the full template is written to `answer.txt`. Here's the shape of it:

**Front Matter** — cover, how-to-read, natal chart snapshot with the "Big Three" summary box.

**Part One — Birth Chart (personality)**
- **Section 1: The Top Three** — dedicated breakdown of Sun (core self), Moon (inner world), and Rising (lens/doorway), plus a 1.4 section on how the three work as a system, ending with a personalized "Big Three Portrait."
- **Section 2: Planetary placements** — Mercury through Pluto, the Nodes, and Chiron, each with sign → house → aspects → plain-English summary, plus angles deep dive and a Planet-by-House master grid covering every house meaning.
- **Section 3: The Four Elements** — closes the birth chart section as requested: weighting/counting method, then Fire/Earth/Air/Water with balanced expression, **excess** and **lack** meanings and balancing advice for each, modality quick-read, and a synthesis "Element Portrait."

**Part Two — Synastry (mirrored structure for parity)**
- Section 5: romantic partners — core markers (Sun–Sun, Moon–Moon, Venus–Mars, etc.), deeper Saturn/Pluto/Neptune/Uranus/Chiron/Node currents, house overlays, red flags, ideal partner profile.
- Section 6: **friends get the exact same architecture** — friendship-specific markers (Mercury–Mercury, Sun–Jupiter, Moon–Venus, soft Saturn), 3rd/5th/9th/11th house overlays, friend red flags, ideal friend profile, with an explicit statement that friendship carries equal weight.
- Section 7: side-by-side synthesis table of partner vs. friend markers.

**Part Three — Transits (personalized year ahead)**
- Section 8: transit method + year-at-a-glance heat map, eclipse/retrograde flags.
- Section 9: **52 weekly entries (Weeks 1–52)** organized month by month, each with a fixed mini-template: week number + date range, theme title, sky this week, personalized natal application, focus area, best/caution days, one action step, reflection prompt. Includes rules for retrograde, eclipse, and quiet weeks.
- Section 10–11: quarterly deep dives and year-end synthesis.

**Back Matter** — glossaries and quick-reference tables (planet×sign, planet×house, aspects, elements, retrograde/eclipse calendars), calculation method notes, and next-step upsells.

Each section is scoped so it can be auto-generated from birth data: fixed slots for computed values, and narrative templates around them. A summary table at the end maps every requirement to its section.
